new_statements.translation: Sissala orthography marks high tones with an acute accent and leaves low tones unmarked: báálɔ 'man', bɔ́tɔ́ 'bag'. [Bender: 'Sissala is a tone language with two tone levels, only high tone being marked in the orthography. Sissala has predominantly CV(C) syllable structure. The language has ATR vowel harmony.']
new_statements.citation: Zalvé, Marc, Lukas Neukom & Michèle Bender (eds.). 2013. Lexique sissala–français avec un index français–sissala. Ouagadougou: ANTBA & SIL Burkina Faso. Introduction (L. Neukom & M. Zalvé), p. 5. Corroborated by Bender 2012:14 and Hartell 1993 (Sissala page).
new_statements.locator: Introduction, p. 5 (PDF page 5), first paragraph under the dialect map; secondary: Bender 2012 §1.4 p.14
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Primary quote: opened (149 pp., LibreOffice 2013, author 'Neukom') and rendered p.5 at 150 dpi. Directly under the dialect map the page reads, verbatim: 'L'orthographe sissala marque les tons hauts par un accent aigu ´ et laisse les tons bas non marqués : báálɔ homme, bɔ́tɔ́ sac.' -- exactly as reported (the extracted text layer garbles the second example as 'bɔɩ́tɔɩ́', as the first reader noted; the page image has bɔ́tɔ́). I read the whole introduction (pp.4-10: alphabet, long vowels, tone marking, noun genres A-G, five verb forms, word classes incl. ideophones 'consonnes finales allongées, redoublements'); the only prosodic content is the H/L tone-marking sentence; a grep of the full 149-…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sissala of Burkina Faso is described as a two-level (H/L) tone language; none of the accessible first-hand descriptions says anything about word stress or accent placement — no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement exists in the accessible sources).
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical tone and its orthographic marking; word-level stress/accent is simply not discussed. Reference dialect of the Lexique is Boura (buuní), the same dialect as Blass's work.
new_statements.identity_note: All quoted statements concern Sissala of Burkina Faso [sld] = siss1242, reference dialect Boura (buuní), Sissili Province — the same variety as Blass's work. Two frequently conflated resources were checked and EXCLUDED as different languages: Blass (ed.) 1975 Sisaala–English dictionary and the Webonary 'Sisaala Dictionary' (both Tumu/Isaalin = Tumulung Sisaala [sil], Ghana), and Moran 2006/2008/2009 (Western Sisaala [ssl], west2465). PHOIBLE's two siss1242 inventories both derive from Hartell 1993 (AA).

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Only prosodic statement (p.5): orthography marks high tones with an acute accent and leaves low tones unmarked (báálɔ 'homme', bɔ́tɔ́ 'sac'); alphabet and vowel-length inventory given (p.4). Reference dialect: Boura (buuní).
